clue.text: Directs one to end thus missing start in short stay

indicators.note: to end says the letter for one is shifted to the end of the word

parts.note: to train something, a gun or a camera, is to direct or aim it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: missing its start means losing the first letter

parts.note: hence means thus or therefore

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone on a brief visit, apparently omitting how things begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to end' moves the I of TRAINS to the back, making TRANSI; 'missing start' cuts HENCE to ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Transience is the quality of lasting only briefly, so a short stay or passing visit illustrates it.

clue.text: Mark, kind in print

definitions.meaning: a distinguishing mark or emblem, as in a symbol stamped on something
to produce printed text on a keyboard

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word; the surface reads like a description of a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word covers a sort or category, a distinguishing symbol, and the act of producing printed text with a keyboard.

clue.text: In a garden building, husband becomes problem, it's claimed

indicators.note: the husband's letter turns into the problem, a straight swap

parts.note: taken as written
a shed is a hut in the garden
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A man in his shed is said to have become a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a title or power is to take or claim it for oneself.

clue.text: Substitute good gold, for German the regular instruction

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute
or is gold in heraldry
der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A bank or mint is told to swap one gold for another, for a German client.
explanation.walkthrough: A standing order is a British term for an instruction to a bank to make a regular fixed payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is a repeated, fixed instruction, typically to a bank to pay a set sum at intervals.

clue.text: Agent soon left out embracing young lady

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps itself around the young lady
the letter for left is taken out of the word

parts.note: early can mean soon, before long
a miss is a young woman

explanation.surface: An agent leaves early, hugging a girl on the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a mission as an agent or representative of another.

clue.text: Christopher Pine, initially in audition is firm

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the sound of the pieces is what counts

parts.note: Chris is the short form of Christopher, followed by the first letter of Pine

explanation.surface: The actor Chris Pine is said to be resolute at a casting call.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Pine is an American film actor, which makes 'audition' fit the surface; the sound of CHRIS P is spelt as a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crispy food is firm and brittle rather than soft, so firm is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Pressure before argument in part of boat

indicators.note: the pressure letter comes ahead of the argument

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Pressure leads to a quarrel aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the pointed front section of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Plump upon answer for building without corners

indicators.note: in a down clue, the plump word sits on top of the answer letter

parts.note: rotund means round and plump

explanation.surface: A tubby figure sits upon a round structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, often domed, so it has no angles to it.

clue.text: A general style underpins laundry

indicators.note: in a down clue the style word lies underneath the laundry

parts.note: washing is clothes to be laundered
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: A general's sense of style rests on his clean clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton is an old word for fashionable style, as in 'the bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was commander of the Continental Army before becoming president, so he is a general.

clue.text: A time fool sent back food in trat?

indicators.note: the three pieces are read in reverse order, back to front

parts.note: taken as written
a sap is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A diner who is slow to order sends back a dish in an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A trat is short for trattoria, an informal Italian restaurant; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the classic dish served in an Italian eatery, an example rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Enjoying success, I consumed seconds for starters

parts.note: to be in it is to be doing well, in the running
taken as written
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A diner boasts of winning by eating second helpings before the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiates are newcomers just admitted to a group, people starting out, so starters works as a noun.

clue.text: Nuts are replicable? Unique!

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material, taken as written

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the idea something can be copied: it is one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irreplaceable cannot be substituted, because there is nothing else like it.

clue.text: Way to conduct dinosaur demo, horribly consuming pterodactyl's head

indicators.note: the jumble swallows the extra letter
a horrible demo is a mangled one, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material, taken as written

indicators.note: only the first letter of the flying reptile is taken

parts.note: the first letter is P

explanation.surface: A museum demonstration of dinosaurs goes horribly wrong when a flying reptile eats someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Modus operandi is Latin for method of working, so it is a way of conducting things.

clue.text: City fails to secure backer

indicators.note: the failing word holds the backer tight inside

parts.note: loses means fails, comes off worse
an angel is a financial backer, especially of a stage show

explanation.surface: A city cannot find an investor for its project.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles is a major city in California, home of Hollywood.

clue.text: Soldiers advanced tracks around delta in plain

indicators.note: the soldiers and the advanced letter go round the delta and the in

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
delta is the radio code word for D
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on tracks

explanation.surface: Troops push forward along tracks around a river delta onto open plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like flat land in a military surface, but it is the adjective meaning unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and plain both mean unremarkable, with nothing special or fancy about it.

clue.text: Small fender bender arose

parts.note: a prang is British slang for a minor car crash, which is what a fender bender is in American English

explanation.surface: A minor car collision occurred.
explanation.walkthrough: Prang is British slang for a small crash or bump in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is a past tense of spring, as in to spring up, meaning to come into being.

clue.text: Spreads denunciation, son demoted in investigation

parts.note: a ban in the old sense is a curse or formal denunciation

indicators.note: demoted means moved down, and in a down clue the son letter drops to the bottom

parts.note: a quest is a search or inquiry
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Rumours of condemnation spread as a son is pushed down the ranks during an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demoted' suits a down clue: the son drops from the top of the investigation word to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is informal for a lavish meal, and banquets are grand feasts.

clue.text: 27 found in Italian chorus

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters of these two words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Italian and the start of chorus

explanation.surface: A newsreader turns up in an Italian choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27-across, NEWSREADER.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter of a news programme, so an example of a newsreader.

clue.text: Slope around hospital room

indicators.note: the slope surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: camber is the slight slope of a road surface

explanation.surface: A sloping road runs around a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a private or official one.

clue.text: Berliner's agreed return of single friend is means to spice things up?

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: the single and friend words are read backwards

parts.note: one means single
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A German agrees that a returning single friend will liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeño is a hot chilli pepper, used in cooking to add heat; the question mark marks a cryptic definition.

clue.text: Tempted, aim to retain the Yorkshire reserve

indicators.note: the aim keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t'
ice is reserve, coolness of manner

explanation.surface: Someone is lured into keeping the Yorkshire stiff upper lip.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speakers famously clip 'the' to t', as in 'down t' pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticed means lured or tempted by an offer of something attractive.

clue.text: Soft fabric to catch one fish

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: the fabric traps the one inside it, as a net would

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: A delicate net of fabric is used to catch a single fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish, so an example of a fish.

clue.text: Angler quit Don, ludicrous and bombastic

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd, so the letters are put into a nonsensical new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fisherman walked out on his boss, who was absurd and pompous.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiloquent language is pompous and inflated, which is what bombastic means.

clue.text: Addict in deception, right to the end

indicators.note: the letter for right is taken from the front and placed at the end

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: An addict is deceptive right up to the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is informal for someone who takes drugs, a drug addict.

clue.text: Unrestrained, Wooster almost enters row

indicators.note: the shortened name goes into the row word

parts.note: a line is a row

indicators.note: the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is the hapless hero of P G Wodehouse's comic novels

explanation.surface: Bertie Wooster, a Wodehouse toff, nearly walks into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, very Wooster, but it is a line in the sense of a row of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Libertine as an adjective means dissolute, free from moral restraint.

clue.text: County resists American cash

definitions.meaning: The usual short form of Buckinghamshire, an English county
to buck a trend is to resist it

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings; Buckinghamshire is a county just north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is a county abbreviation, a verb for opposing something, and US slang for money.

clue.text: Rank smell obviously repels them at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of these four words is taken

parts.note: the four words supply their opening letters in order

explanation.surface: A foul odour clearly drives people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul-smelling, matching the surface, but it is the verb to arrange in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To sort things is to arrange them into order or classes, the same as ranking them.

clue.text: Bruce, for one, running wee errands

indicators.note: running errands sounds natural, but here running means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Bruce does small odd jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiona Bruce is a long-serving BBC television news presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona Bruce presented BBC news bulletins for many years, so she is an example of the broadcaster category.
